Abstract
Code review, which aims at ensuring the over-
all quality and reliability of software, is a cor-
nerstone of software development. Unfortu-
nately, while crucial, Code review is a labor-
intensive process that the research community
is looking to automate.
Existing aut

summary.text: Title block, authors and the start of the abstract of the CodeAgent paper by Xunzhu Tang, Kisub Kim, Yewei Song, Cedric Lothritz, Bei Li, Saad Ezzini, Haoye Tian (corresponding author), Jacques Klein and Tegawendé F. Bissyandé (University of Luxembourg, Singapore Management University, Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology, Northeastern University, Lancaster University, University of Melbourne). Code review is labour-intensive, and existing automated methods use single input-output generative models that struggle to emulate its collaborative nature; CodeAgent is a multi-agent LLM system for code review with a supervisory agent, QA-Checker, that keeps every agent's contribution on the initial review question. Introduction
Code review (Bacchelli and Bird, 2013; Bosu and
Carver, 2013; Davila and Nunes, 2021) imple-
ments a process wherein software maintainers ex-
amine and assess code contributions to ensure
quality and adherence to coding standards, and
identify potential bugs or improvements. In recent
literature, various approaches (Tufano et al., 2021,
20

summary.text: The end of the abstract and the introduction. The evaluation covers the remaining tasks, format coherence and code revision suggestions, and the authors report a new state of the art; data and code are on GitHub. Most code review automation rewrites submitted code and ignores the interactive, collaborative nature of review, which spans vulnerability detection, formatting and revision consistency. CodeAgent simulates a review team (authors, reviewers, decision makers), and its QA-Checker addresses prompt drifting, where multi-agent or chain-of-thought conversations stray from the topic, by refining questions and realigning answers. Contributions claimed are the first autonomous agent-based system for practical code review, a new dataset of 3,545 real-world code changes and commit messages, and a demonstration of QA-Checker. Headline results: a 41% increase in vulnerability hit rate, 3 to 7 percentage points more vulnerabilities than GPT-4 and CodeBERT, about 14% higher inconsistency recall than ReAct, and about 30% better average Edit Progress on code revision.

2.1
Tasks
We define CA, VA, FA, and CR in as following:
CA (Zhang et al., 2022): Consistency analysis be-
tween code change and commit message; the task
is to detect cases where the commit message ac-
curate describes (in natural language) the intent of
code changes (in programming language).
VA (Braz et al., 2022): Vulnerability analysis; the
task is to identify cases where the code change in-
troduces a vulnerability in the code.
FA (Han et al., 2020): Format consistency analysis
between commit and original files;

summary.text: Tasks and pipeline (with Figures 1 and 2). The four tasks are consistency analysis between code change and commit message (CA), vulnerability analysis (VA), format consistency analysis between the commit and the original files (FA), and code revision suggestions (CR). Six roles (User, CEO, CTO, CPO, Reviewer, Coder) work through four sequential phases in a waterfall: Basic Info Sync, where CEO, CTO and Coder identify the input's modality and language; Code Review, where the Reviewer, helped by the Coder, writes consistency, security and format analyses with revision suggestions; Code Alignment, where the Coder revises the code with the Reviewer; and Document, where CEO, CPO, Coder and Reviewer summarise the review. Each phase is a series of atomic two-agent conversations in instructor-assistant style, each supervised by QA-Checker until requirements are met or the turn limit is reached.

summary.text: QA-Checker (Figure 3). An instruction-driven agent checks each answer against its question; if the first answer a0 is inappropriate for the initial instruction q0, it attaches an additional instruction and forms a new question q1 = CB(q0 + aai0), repeating until the answer is judged appropriate or the maximum number of turns is reached. A new dataset of over 3,545 commits and 2,933 pull requests from more than 180 projects in nine languages (Python, Java, Go, C++, JavaScript, C, C#, PHP, Ruby) targets consistency and format detection, with positive and negative samples split by whether pull requests were merged or closed (for CA, 2,089 and 820 consistent against 501 and 135 inconsistent). summary.text: Vulnerability analysis (Table 2, Figure 4). VA covers more than 25 vulnerability types, and because few commits are labelled, the ground truth was built by running CodeAgent on the 3,545 samples and manually verifying what it found, over 120 hours with each sample checked by a researcher and an engineer; CodeBERT (frozen) and GPT were then applied as binary predictors. CodeAgent's 449 confirmed of 483 found gives a 92.96% confirmation rate, against 19.94% for CodeBERT, 36.69% for GPT-3.5 and 51.42% for GPT-4.0, which the authors partly attribute to GPT-4's longer context. Figure 4 shows the overlaps: CodeAgent's confirmed set contains all of CodeBERT's 212 and GPT-3.5's 317 and 334 of GPT-4.0's 345. In the ablation, removing QA-Checker lowers both hit rates (73.23% and 11.65%).

blocks.title: Conclusion
blocks.content:
In this paper, we introduced CodeAgent, a novel
multi-agent framework that automates code re-
views.
CodeAgent leverages its novel QA-
Checker system to maintain focus on the re-
view’s objectives and ensure alignment. Our ex-
periments demonstrate CodeAgent’s effective-
ness in detecting vulnerabilities, enforcing code-
message consistency, and promoting uniform code
style. Furthermore, CodeAgent outperforms ex-
isting state-of-the-art solutions in code revision
suggestions.
By incorporating human-like con-
versational elements and considering the specific
characteristics of code review, Code

summary.text: Conclusion, limitations, ethics statement and references. CodeAgent, a multi-agent code review framework kept on task by QA-Checker, is reported to detect vulnerabilities, check code-message consistency and format alignment, and outperform prior code revision tools. Limitations named are uncertain generalisability to other development environments and industries, and a baseline test that may be insufficient, possibly overestimating the system on edge cases. The ethics statement notes no human participants and only public data. The references cover code review studies and tools, code models, multi-agent LLM frameworks and prompting methods.

Algorithmic Description of CodeAgent

summary.text: The appendix table of contents, Appendix A and Appendix B. Appendix A states a lemma: if QA-Checker's quality function Q of a question-answer pair is twice differentiable with a positive definite Hessian, and questions are refined by attaching instructions, the sequence of pairs converges to an optimal pair under regularity conditions; the authors argue this from a second-order Taylor expansion with a Newton-style answer update and a small learning rate. In practice QA-Checker compares Q with a threshold and adds an instruction when it falls below; Q is an equally weighted sum of relevance (cosine similarity of question and answer vectors), specificity (technicality of content words per word) and coherence (discourse connectives, coreference consistency, answer-pattern adherence). Appendix B gives the full related work on code review automation and collaborative AI.

QA-Checker is specialised for question-answer tasks with precise execution, while recursive self-improvement systems have broader scope, multi-level learning and integrate experience across projects; the authors argue QA-Checker's specialisation suits role conversations, where accuracy, relevance and clarity of each response matter.

blocks.title: Conclusion

broad adaptability and systemic learning, the QA-

tasks, particularly in role conversations.
Its fo-

its efficiency in handling conversational nuances
make it an essential component in AI-driven com-
munication systems.
